anim_aide_html:
Animations

The ClassAction teaching animations of the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, originally written in Flash, remade in Python for Windows, macOS and Linux. All 92 animations of the catalogue are available, sorted by topic; those that were only movies have become simulations. Added to them are, in “Ancient astronomy”, the Antikythera Mechanism in 3D, adapted from Anticythere3D, by the same author (crank turned with the mouse, dials engraved in Greek, open or exploded machine, exact gear ratios; full application: github.com/ARP273-ROSE/Anticythere3D), and, in “Interstellar Medium and Star Formation”, Orion in 3D: the constellation unfolded to its true distances, with its clouds, the Orion Nebula and the Horsehead, and a dive with ESO and Hubble images.

Hover data sheets

In Orion in 3D, Big Dipper 3D, the Big Dipper clock, heliacal rising, the coordinate systems comparison and the HR diagram, hovering over (or touching) a star or a nebula opens its data sheet, laid next to it: name, type, magnitudes, distance and its uncertainty, temperature, radius, luminosity, and the source of each value (SIMBAD, Gaia DR3, Hipparcos, papers). With the keyboard: Tab goes from one object to the next, brightest first, so do the arrows while a sheet is open, Escape closes it; the summary is read by screen readers. Real stars have their true colour (black body at their temperature, CIE 1931).

Spectra

The Spectrum Explorer and the Spectroscopic Parallax compute the lines (Saha–Boltzmann on model atmospheres, 133 NIST lines, TiO and CH molecular bands, Planck continuum); extrapolated cases and the former absolute-magnitude calibration are flagged.

Handling

  • Dragging a sphere rotates it (the grabbed point follows the mouse); dragging a star, the Moon, the Earth or an observer moves it. What the mouse does in each animation is recalled in small print below the scene.
  • Play / Pause and Speed (0.1 to 10 ×) run the time; Reset goes back to the initial state.
  • Each setting has a slider and a numeric field; computed values are shown below the settings.
  • Settings are kept from one session to the next.
  • Web version ↗ opens the animation, with its settings, in Coupole Web (arp273-rose.github.io/coupole-web), in a browser, on a computer, tablet or phone.

Rendering

Sun, Moon, Earth and planets as shaded spheres (night side turned away from the Sun), typeset formulas (fractions, superscripts, subscripts, radicals; STIX Two Math font), labels placed without overlapping. Daylight simulator: Natural Earth coastlines, equirectangular or polar (North or South Pole) projection, or a 3D globe rotated with the mouse (wheel: zoom; double-click: face the subsolar point). Eclipse shadow simulator: “Replay an eclipse” shows each of the 133 eclipses of the 2015–2044 table to true scale.

Computations

Sidereal time (IAU 1982), obliquity (IAU 2006), position of the Sun and equation of time (Meeus, 0.01° accuracy), coordinate changes, Kepler’s equation, distance modulus, shadow cones, mean lunar phases and nodes of the lunar orbit (eclipse seasons), precession, equilibrium tides, synodic periods, Newton’s gravitation, Stefan-Boltzmann law and IAU solar constants, Planck’s and Wien’s laws, hydrogen levels, refraction and Fresnel formulas, Doppler effect through the retarded time, radial velocities, transits and eclipses (exact overlap area of the discs), barycenter of the Solar System, energy budgets of the fusion reactions: checked with SageMath, astropy and ERFA (see the manual, Animations chapter). The empirical calibrations of the original (spectral type, bolometric corrections, HR diagram sequences) are kept as they are; the real data (exoplanets, planets, eclipsing binaries, spectra) cite their source in the NOTICE file.

anim_spectrum010_echelle_aide: Teaching contrast (default): lines widened to 0.8 nm and deepened (ratio to the continuum cubed) so that they can be seen, as on a demonstration spectrum; realistic scale: computed depths and widths, often barely visible (the Sun).
anim_spectrum010_e_pedago_v: teaching contrast: lines widened (0.8 nm) and deepened (ratio to the continuum cubed)
anim_spectrum010_contraste_note: Teaching contrast: lines enhanced to be visible (“Lines” setting).

anim_aide_fiche: Hover over or touch a star or a nebula: its data sheet (values and sources); with the keyboard, Tab goes from one object to the next (brightest first), so do the arrows while a sheet is open, Escape closes it.
anim_hrexplorer_couleur_t_aide: Each star takes the colour of a black body at its temperature (CIE 1931 → sRGB); its outline keeps the colour of its group. Unticked: group colour.
anim_bigdipper_source_v: parallaxes adopted by SIMBAD (Hipparcos 2007, Gaia), retrieved on 14/10/2026
anim_orion3d_b_face_aide: Looks at Orion from the Earth: the projections on the celestial sphere draw the constellation.
anim_orion3d_b_cote_aide: The Earth at the bottom, Orion at the top: each star at its distance.
anim_orion3d_unite_aide: Unit of the distances written next to the stars: light-years or parsecs (1 pc = 3.26 ly).
anim_orion3d_lignes_aide: From the Earth to each star: seen from the Earth, each star lies somewhere along its line of sight.
anim_orion3d_noms_aide: Name of each star, of M42 and of the Horsehead, with its distance.
anim_orion3d_sphere_aide: Projection of each star on the celestial sphere, where the figure of Orion appears as we see it.
anim_orion3d_figure_aide: The lines of the figure (Stellarium, “modern” sky) between the stars at their distance: from the side, they join stars that nothing links.
anim_orion3d_nebuleuses_aide: The Orion Nebula (blister hollowed into the OMC-1 cloud, Trapezium, Veil) and IC 434 (red front lit by σ Ori, Horsehead pillar, edge of Orion B) at their exact position, enlarged to be visible.
anim_orion3d_agrandi: M42 and IC 434: size enlarged ×{k}, exact position and distance; shape of M42 beyond 0.5 pc and depth of IC 434 schematic
anim_orion3d_nuages_aide: Published skeletons of the giant molecular clouds Orion A and Orion B (Zucker et al. 2021).
anim_orion3d_barres_aide: Uncertainty of each measured distance, along the line of sight (Alnilam, Mintaka, Meissa and Hatysa, placed at the distance of their group, have none: their own measurement is in the values).
anim_orion3d_accentuees_aide: Boosts the saturation of the true colours, pale to the eye (teaching choice, off by default).
anim_orion3d_brutes_aide: Alnilam, Mintaka, Meissa and Hatysa at their own (very uncertain) parallax instead of the published distance of their star group.
anim_orion3d_d_publiees: published (Alnilam, Mintaka, Meissa, Hatysa: distance of their group)
anim_orion3d_souris: Drag: turn the scene (face-on: the figure in the sky; from the side: the depths); double-click: back; wheel or pinch: zoom.
anim_orion3d_adapte: Coupole’s own (not in ClassAction): SIMBAD, Gaia DR3, Hipparcos 2007 and papers cited in the data sheets

classe_carte_aide: Open the module: questions, animations, outlines, tables and images
classe_accueil_texte: 22 modules: questions to discuss in groups, interactive animations, outlines, tables and images. Your progress, modules and settings are kept on this computer (and can be exchanged with Coupole Web through a file).
classe_aide_html:
Modules

The “Modules” button opens the home page: the 22 ClassAction modules (and two bonus modules), “My modules” and the resumption of the last question. A module page has Questions, Animations, Outlines, Tables, Images tabs; double-click or Enter opens an item; an outline, table or image opens in its own window (several at once); hovering over an item shows a preview; right click: “Add to…” one of your modules.

Question: “Adapt question” menus, choices A, B, C… (keys A to H), “Check” (Enter) records the attempt, “Show answer” (R) makes the right answer flash orange, “Hint” (I), “New draw” (N), left and right arrows: previous or next question, F: full screen. Resources related to the question are marked ★: on the right in a wide window, in the “★ n” menu of the header in a narrow one.

“My progress”: summary per module, questions to review, export and import the backup (file shared with Coupole Web), reset all or part (a copy is kept before erasing, then “Undo”).
